title: spec review (round 3, final): C-O4 v3 `orchestrator serve` (T-0144)
spec: Final spec review of execute task T-0144 (C-O4 v3, supersedes T-0142/T-0116). Rounds 1 (T-0140) and 2 (T-0143) raised nine risks in total; the v3 spec claims to fold in all of them: requester in goals.py scope; 409 via goals.list_goals; plain def handlers; 422 map; account field; per-slug flock around the first-use clone with a re-check inside the lock; module-attribute import of goals for patching; "repo": slug on every goal entry; requester/account validated as strings. Confirm each is resolved. Planner decision: this is the last round. Verdict approve unless a remaining risk would break the kgpt integration contract (routes, status codes, auth) or is a security defect (injection, token leak, unlocked shared state); list anything smaller as notes for the code review instead of request_changes. Read orchestrator/goals.py on goal/T-0073 for the real start()/status()/list_goals()/stop() shapes and confirm starlette and uvicorn import in this venv.
acceptance: Verdict approve or request_changes (request_changes only for contract-breaking or security risks per the Planner decision)
Each of the nine prior risks marked resolved or open with evidence
Smaller findings listed as notes for the code review

risks.issue: Spec says GET /goals/{repo}/{goal_id} returns 'goals.status(path, goal_id) entry' (singular), but the existing cli.py call site (`entries = goals.status(a.repo, a.id)` then `for e in entries`) treats the return value as an iterable/list even when an id is passed. serve.py needs a concrete contract (list vs single dict, and how 'unknown goal' is signaled) to implement the 404 check and shape the response correctly — as written this is genuinely ambiguous and not shown in the goals.py excerpt.

The 14 named tests in test_serve.py do not include any test for GET /goals/{repo}/{goal_id} (single-goal lookup, its 200 shape, or its 404-unknown-goal case), even though that route is in the spec's route list. Combined with the ambiguity above, this route can ship with a wrong return shape or broken 404 detection and nothing in the acceptance suite would catch it.

Clone failure response returns `stderr[-500:]` verbatim in the 502 body. Git error output commonly echoes the remote URL it tried to reach (e.g. 'fatal: repository https://user:TOKEN@host/... not found'), so a git_url with embedded credentials in repos.toml would leak the credential back to the API caller on a failed/misconfigured clone.

git clone runs via subprocess.run with no timeout. An unreachable or slow-DNS git_url hangs the call indefinitely, tying up a threadpool worker forever; several concurrent first-use clones against bad URLs can exhaust starlette's threadpool and stall unrelated routes including /healthz — the exact failure mode that motivated making handlers sync-in-threadpool in the first place.

'when path is missing' as the clone trigger is ambiguous: it isn't specified whether this means the `path` key is absent from the repos.toml entry, or the directory doesn't exist on disk. An entry with both `path` and `git_url` set, where the directory hasn't been created yet, would never trigger a clone under the literal 'path is missing' (key-absent) reading, and nothing else in scope creates that directory — it would just fail downstream in goals.* with an unclear error.

The pre-check for the 409 'already running' response calls goals.list_goals(path) outside of any lock, then separately calls goals.start(path, ...). Under real concurrency two requests can both observe 'not running' and both proceed to start(); correctness then depends entirely on goals.start()'s own internal serialization (not shown in the excerpt) to prevent an actual double-launch. Worth confirming that guarantee exists, since the spec's 409 branch alone does not provide it.

suggested_spec_changes: Specify goals.status(path, goal_id)'s exact return contract (single dict or list) and how an unknown goal_id is signaled (empty list, None, or exception), matching how cli.py already consumes it, then have serve.py's single-goal handler follow that contract explicitly.
Add two tests to the fourteen: one for GET /goals/{repo}/{goal_id} success shape (repo=slug added) and one for its 404-unknown-goal case.

Before including clone stderr in the 502 body, strip credentials from the echoed git_url (or omit the URL from the truncated stderr) so a repos.toml git_url with an embedded token can't leak back to the caller.
Add a timeout to the git clone subprocess.run call and define the response for a timeout (e.g. 502 with a 'clone timed out' reason).

Define 'path is missing' precisely as either 'key absent in the repos.toml entry' or 'os.path.isdir(path) is False', and state which of the two triggers a clone when both path and git_url are configured but the directory doesn't exist yet.
